'''Jarnell D'Marcus Stokes''' (born January 7, 1994) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee Volunteers]]. He was one of the top rated high school players in the class of 2011. He was selected in with the 35th overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]] by the [[Utah Jazz]], and later traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].

==High school career==
Stokes was ranked as the No. 11 overall prospect by [[Rivals.com]] and No. 18 by [[ESPN.com]]. As a junior at [[Central High School (Memphis, Tennessee)|Central High School]], he averaged 17.2 points and 9.2 rebounds per game.<ref name=bio>{{cite news|title=Jarnell Stokes Bio|url=http://www.utsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/jarnell_stokes_790793.html|access-date=June 26, 2014|work=UTSports.com|archive-date=November 29, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141129043820/http://www.utsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/jarnell_stokes_790793.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Stokes chose Tennessee over offers from Arkansas, Connecticut, Florida, Kentucky, Memphis, and Ole Miss.<ref>{{cite news|title=Jarnell Stokes Recruiting Profile|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/102645/jarnell-stokes|access-date=November 25, 2015|work=ESPN.com}}</ref>

==College career==
Stokes played three collegiate seasons at the [[University of Tennessee]], averaging 13.0 points, 9.6 rebounds and 1.08 blocks on .530 shooting in 29.7 minutes in 87 games. He left the [[Tennessee Volunteers men's basketball|Volunteers]] ranked fourth in school history in double-doubles (40), eighth in total rebounds (836) and 14th in blocks (94). He also led the [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] in offensive rebounding in 2013 and 2014.<ref name="bio" />

==Professional career==

===Memphis Grizzlies (2014–2015)===
On June 26, 2014, Stokes was selected with the 35th overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]] by the [[Utah Jazz]]. He was later traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] on draft night.<ref>{{cite news|title=Grizzlies acquire draft rights to Jarnell Stokes|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-acquire-jarnell-stokes-140626|access-date=June 26, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=June 26, 2014}}</ref> In July 2014, he joined the Grizzlies for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]] before going on to sign a multi-year deal with the franchise on August 18, 2014.<ref>{{cite news|title=Grizzlies sign Jarnell Stokes to multi-year contract|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-sign-jarnell-stokes-140818|access-date=August 18, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=August 18, 2014}}</ref> On December 3, 2014, he scored a season-high 12 points in a loss to the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Harden leads Rockets over Grizzlies 105-96|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141203/MEMHOU/gameinfo.html|access-date=December 3, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=December 3, 2014}}</ref> During his rookie season, he had multiple assignments with the [[Iowa Energy]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=All-Time NBA Assignments|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/all-time-nba-assignments/|access-date=December 12, 2014|work=NBA.com}}</ref>

===Miami Heat (2015–2016)===
On November 10, 2015, Stokes was traded, along with [[Beno Udrih]], to the [[Miami Heat]] in exchange for [[Mario Chalmers]] and [[James Ennis (basketball)|James Ennis]].<ref>{{cite news|title=HEAT Acquire Beno Udrih and Jarnell Stokes|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-acquire-beno-udrih-and-jarnell-stokes|access-date=November 10, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=November 10, 2015}}</ref> The move reunited him with former Tennessee teammate [[Josh Richardson]]. On January 20, 2016, he made his debut for the Heat in a 106–87 loss to the [[Washington Wizards]], recording four points in five minutes.<ref>{{cite web|title=Wall, Beal each score 18, Wizards down Heat, 106-87|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160120/MIAWAS/gameinfo.html|access-date=January 20, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=February 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160121050613/http://www.nba.com/games/20160120/MIAWAS/gameinfo.html|archive-date=January 21, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

During his sophomore season, he received multiple assignments to the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]], the Heat's [[NBA Development League|D-League]] affiliate.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/assignments/ |title=2015-16 NBA Assignments |work=NBA.com |access-date=December 25, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150906020056/http://dleague.nba.com/news/assignments/ |archive-date=September 6, 2015 }}</ref> On January 29, 2016, he was named in the East All-Star team for the 2016 [[NBA Development League All-Star Game|NBA D-League All-Star Game]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/2016-nba-development-league-all-star-game-rosters/|title=Sixteen NBA Veterans Headline Rosters for NBA Development League All-Star Game Presented By Kumho Tire|work=NBA.com|date=January 29, 2016|access-date=January 29, 2016|archive-date=February 7, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170207115139/http://dleague.nba.com/news/2016-nba-development-league-all-star-game-rosters/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On February 18, 2016, Stokes was traded, along with cash considerations, to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in exchange for a conditional 2018 second-round pick.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-acquire-jarnell-stokes|title=Pelicans Acquire Jarnell Stokes|work=NBA.com|date=February 18, 2016|access-date=February 18, 2016}}</ref> He was waived by the Pelicans the next day.<ref>{{cite news|title=Pelicans Sign Bryce Dejean-Jones|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-bryce-dejean-jones-0|access-date=February 19, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=February 19, 2016}}</ref>

===Sioux Falls Skyforce (2016)===
On February 27, 2016, Stokes was acquired by the Sioux Falls Skyforce.<ref>{{cite news|title=Skyforce Acquire Jarnell Stokes|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/skyforce-acquire-jarnell-stokes/n-5105180|access-date=February 27, 2016|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=February 27, 2016}}</ref> He helped the Skyforce win an NBA D-League-record 40 games in 2015–16, securing the first seed in the Eastern Conference playoffs. In 28 regular season games, he averaged team highs of 20.6 points and 9.3 rebounds per game. He subsequently earned [[NBA Development League Most Valuable Player Award|league MVP]] honors.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/jarnell-stokes-2015-16-nba-dleague-mvp/|title=Jarnell Stokes Named 2015-16 NBA Development League MVP|work=NBA.com|date=April 14, 2016|access-date=April 14, 2016}}</ref> Stokes went on to help the Skyforce cap off a historic season with a playoff run that ended in a 2–1 Finals series victory over the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]]. He added to his regular season MVP award by garnering the [[NBA Development League Finals Most Valuable Player Award|Finals MVP]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20160427/LADSXF/|title=Sioux Falls Skyforce Cap Historic Season with First NBA D-League|work=NBA.com|date=April 27, 2016|access-date=April 27, 2016|archive-date=April 28, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160428121154/http://dleague.nba.com/games/20160427/LADSXF/|url-status=dead}}</ref> as well as earning [[All-NBA Development League Team|All-NBA D-League First Team]] honors.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/2015-16-all-nba-dleague-teams-release/|title=NBA Development League Announces 2015-16 All-NBA D-League Teams|work=NBA.com|date=April 29, 2016|access-date=April 30, 2016|archive-date=September 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160904054918/http://dleague.nba.com/news/2015-16-all-nba-dleague-teams-release/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Denver Nuggets (2016)===
In July 2016, Stokes joined the [[San Antonio Spurs]] for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-announce-2016-las-vegas-summer-league-roster/|title=SPURS ANNOUNCE 2016 LAS VEGAS SUMMER LEAGUE ROSTER|work=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2016|access-date=January 3, 2017}}</ref> On September 15, 2016, he signed with the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-four-players-to-contracts-091516|title=Nuggets Sign Four Players to Contracts|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=September 15, 2016|access-date=September 16, 2016}}</ref> On November 15, 2016, he was waived by the Nuggets after appearing in two games.<ref>{{cite news|title=Denver Nuggets Waive Jarnell Stokes|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/waive-jarnell-stokes-111516|access-date=November 16, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=November 15, 2016}}</ref>

===Second stint with Sioux Falls Skyforce (2017)===
On March 23, 2017, Stokes was reacquired by the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://siouxfalls.dleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-reacquire-jarnell-stokes/|title=SKYFORCE REACQUIRE JARNELL STOKES|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=March 23, 2017|access-date=March 26, 2017|archive-date=March 24, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170324092605/http://siouxfalls.dleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-reacquire-jarnell-stokes/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Zhejiang Golden Bulls (2017–2018)===
In July 2017, Stokes signed with the [[Zhejiang Golden Bulls]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Zhejiang Golden Bulls officially announces the signing of Jarnell Stokes|url=https://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/242502/zhejiang-golden-bulls-officially-announces-the-signing-of-jarnell-stokes.html|access-date=November 8, 2017|work=Sportando.com|date=July 27, 2017}}</ref> On February 2, 2018, he was waived by the [[Zhejiang Golden Bulls]].<ref>{{cite news|title=浙江开除斯托克斯 称他是CBA最无职业操守外援|url=http://www.sohu.com/a/220607434_461606|access-date=February 2, 2018|work=Sohu.com|language=zh|date=February 2, 2018}}</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20180203101243/http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2018-02/03/c_136946407.htm CBA side Zhejiang parts ways with former NBA player Stokes, accusing him of "being unprofessional].XINHUANET.com.[2018-02-03].</ref>

===Third stint with Sioux Falls Skyforce (2018)===
On August 27, 2018, Stokes returned to the [[Miami Heat]] on a training camp contract.<ref>{{cite web |title=HEAT Signs Jarnell Stokes |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-signs-jarnell-stokes |website=NBA.com |access-date=August 28, 2018 |date=August 27, 2018}}</ref> He was waived on October 13.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-waives-purvis-putney-stokes-and-weber-181013|title=HEAT Waives Purvis, Putney, Stokes And Weber|work=NBA.com|date=October 13, 2018|access-date=October 14, 2018}}</ref>

On December 8, 2018, Stokes was reacquired by the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/force-acquire-jarnell-stokes/|title=SKYFORCE ACQUIRE JARNELL STOKES|date=December 8, 2018|work=NBA.com|access-date=December 8, 2018|archive-date=December 9, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181209124706/https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/force-acquire-jarnell-stokes/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Memphis Hustle (2019)===
On January 1, 2019, Stokes was signed to a two-way contract by the Memphis Grizzlies, to split time with their G League affiliate, the [[Memphis Hustle]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-jarnell-stokes-190101|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign Jarnell Stokes to two-way contract|date=January 1, 2019|work=NBA.com|access-date=January 1, 2019}}</ref>

===Xinjiang Flying Tigers (2019–2020)===
On February 12, 2019, Stokes was reported to have signed with the [[Xinjiang Flying Tigers]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].<ref>{{cite news|title=前浙江外援替换哈达迪 新疆用尽更换外援名额|url=http://sports.sina.com.cn/basketball/cba/2019-02-12/doc-ihrfqzka5053869.shtml|access-date=February 12, 2019|work=sina.com.cn|language=zh|date=February 12, 2019}}</ref> He debuted with the Flying Tigers on the same day, making a double-double with 30 points, 19 rebounds, 2 blocks and a steal in a 120–115 victory over the [[Shanxi Brave Dragons]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Regular Season Round 40: Xinjiang FT - Shanxi Z. 120-115|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/China/2019/0212_4369_2922.asp|date=February 12, 2019|website=eurobasket.com|access-date=February 12, 2019}}</ref> In July 2019, Stokes returned for the [[2019 NBA Summer League]] to play for the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://allfortennessee.com/2019/07/05/nba-jarnell-stokes-will-participate-nba-summer-league/|title=NBA: Jarnell Stokes will play in the NBA Summer League for Portland|date=July 5, 2019|website=All for Tennessee|language=en-US|access-date=July 13, 2019}}</ref>

On July 23, 2024, Stokes signed with the [[Goyang Sono Skygunners]] of the [[Korean Basketball League]] (KBL).<ref>{{cite web |title=프로농구 소노, 'NBA 출신' 자넬 스톡스 영입... "팬과 즐거운 농구할 것" |url=https://www.chosun.com/sports/basketball/2024/07/23/7U2U3A5W42YBEODADPBHI36O6E/ |publisher=조선일보 |access-date=29 August 2024 |date=23 July 2024}}</ref> However, Stoke violated the contract by not entering South Korea to join the team on the scheduled date.<ref>{{cite web |title=소노 외국인 선수 스톡스, ‘연락 두절’로 KBL 재정위 심의 대상 올라 |url=https://sports.khan.co.kr/article/202409131544013 |publisher=스포츠경향 |access-date=16 September 2024 |date=13 September 2024}}</ref> On September 14, his contract was terminated and replaced by [[D. J. Burns]].<ref>{{cite web |title=프로농구 소노, 미국 대학 무대서 활약한 D.J. 번스 영입 |url=https://www.yna.co.kr/view/AKR20240914047400007 |publisher=연합뉴스 |access-date=16 September 2024 |date=14 September 2024}}</ref> On September 19, Stokes was banned from KBL for following two seasons.<ref>{{cite web |title=KBL, 소노에 ‘노쇼’ 시전한 스톡스에게 2시즌 자격정지 징계 |url=https://jumpball.co.kr/news/newsview.php?ncode=1065602592340574 |publisher=점프볼 |access-date=19 September 2024 |date=19 September 2024}}</ref>
